questions.question: Make sure your wheel bearing and seals are:
questions.explanation: During an inspection, check that wheel bearings and seals are not leaking.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: When you start an engine:

options.text: Warning lights should turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers should go out after a few seconds. If they do not turn off, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when used:

options.text: They will be the most effective.

questions.explanation: If brakes pull to one side when used, this is a sign of brake trouble.

questions.question: When driving, knowing what is happening behind you is:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires knowing what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Use your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: Some water and compressor oil are normally found in an air brake system. This water and compressor oil:

options.text: Are needed for the system to work properly.
Should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: If water and compressor oil build up in an air brake system, the system can be damaged. Air tanks have drains to remove this buildup. You should operate manual drains at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: When making a left turn with two available turn lanes, start the turn in the rightmost lane because:

options.text: It is easier to see turning vehicles on your left than on your right.
Your vehicle will turn more quickly.
Other vehicles will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is easier to see turning vehicles on your left than on your right.
questions.explanation: When making a left turn with more than one turn lane, use the rightmost lane. Large vehicles often swing right to turn left. It is safer to have other left-turning traffic on your left instead of your right. This gives you the best view of other turning vehicles and reduces collision risk.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
Complete it as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps and reduces the chance you will miss something.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, match the speed of surrounding vehicles. Vehicles moving in the same direction at the same speed are less likely to collide. Never exceed legal speed limits.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: Planning realistic travel time helps reduce frustration, which can lead to aggressive driving. Allow extra time for traffic delays. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, not making gestures at other drivers, and keeping both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: When you pull over on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It rarely happens with large trucks.
It usually happens when vehicles go faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a large amount of water on the road for hydroplaning to happen.

questions.question: How should you do an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Go forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then go forward to the left.
Go forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first go forward straight, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: You should not use your mirrors.
You should not use your turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used on the rear tires.
Yes, if carrying a light load.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip check, what should you look for?

options.text: A gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a tractor/trailer connection, look into the fifth wheel gap and make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes at an intersection, which lane should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lane you use.

questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. When two left turn lanes are available, always start your turn in the rightmost lane.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The state will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: If convicted of any traffic violation in any vehicle, you must notify your employer within 30 days. You must also inform your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: When should cargo be checked during a trip?

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. Also check cargo every time you stop for a break. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured during the entire trip.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to apply for a CDL?
questions.explanation: In Vermont, you must be at least 18 years old to get a CDL. To drive across state lines, you must be at least 21 years old.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is allowed?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system
To keep people from breathing the air from the system

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to help stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through water or a large puddle?

options.text: Try to stop in the water

questions.explanation: Avoid large puddles and moving water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift into a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water, mud, and dirt out of the brake system.

questions.question: What are turned on by an electric switch triggered by the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal. The brake pedal activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators?

options.text: Used to add alcohol to air brake systems
Only allowed in northern parts of the state

questions.correctAnswerText: Used to add alcohol to air brake systems
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. They add alcohol to the system to help prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If you drive in fog, slow down and turn on your flashers and low beam headlights. Do not use high beams—they reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

questions.question: What should you NOT use your mirrors for?

options.text: Checking how fast you are going

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking how fast you are going
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when changing lanes, turning, merging, and making tight moves. However, mirrors should not be used to determine your speed—use your speedometer for that.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: The state will notify your employer
Tell your employer within two business days
Tell your employer within a month

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within two business days
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, or if you cannot drive.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test from a police officer?

options.text: You can refuse without any penalty

questions.explanation: Most states have Implied Consent Laws. By driving on public roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Know the laws in every state where you drive.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that slows down a vehicle
A device that reduces vehicle noise
A device that improves fuel economy

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that slows down a vehicle
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow vehicles down. This reduces how much drivers need to use the brakes.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity can:

options.text: Make a vehicle more likely to tip over
Be safely carried in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Make a vehicle more likely to tip over
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. It is important to keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: Why should cargo be covered?

options.text: To protect people if cargo spills

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect people if cargo spills
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people from spills. Covering also protects cargo from weather.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down quickly
Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down in a smooth and gradual way when stopping.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop pumping air into the tanks
Begin pumping air into the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop pumping air into the tanks
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor when air tanks reach about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When traveling downhill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: After you pick up speed going down

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you start going downhill. If you don't start slowly enough, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, the weight over the axles should be:
questions.explanation: Weight on each axle must be neither too light nor too heavy. Poor weight distribution can affect steering, reduce traction, or damage axles.

questions.question: Placards should be used:

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials
When there is extra space on a truck
Only when hazardous materials exceed 200 pounds

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials
questions.explanation: Placards are required on any vehicle carrying hazardous materials. They must be displayed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ at the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check each slack adjuster. Pull them to make sure they move no more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: A truck should be parked so that:

options.text: It must be backed up to leave
It can be pulled forward to leave

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be pulled forward to leave
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery right after it starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Water has not yet washed away the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts. Rainwater creates a slick film when it mixes with oil and grease that has not yet washed away from the road.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Swerve your vehicle out of the way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve your vehicle out of the way if needed.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, what should you do?

options.text: Accept it and drive at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation while driving safely.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should be done about broken suspension parts?

options.text: Repair them, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be repaired immediately.

questions.question: How should you complete a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull forward directly into the space.
Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet.

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually for a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your tires carefully before a trip. Tire sizes must match, and tires cannot be cut, cracked, or damaged.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is:

options.text: Illegal to transport in most states.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable cargo. It has a high center of gravity, and the swinging meat can affect how you control the vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the tire load stated?

options.text: On the side of the tire.
On the inside of the tire.
On the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load is written on the side of each tire. This tells you the maximum safe weight the tire can carry.
